facts_of_case: Matrimonial discord between husband and wife, divorce petition filed, settlement reached, criminal proceeding pending

legal_principles.principle: Power to quash criminal proceedings under Section 482 of the Code is to be exercised sparingly and with caution.
legal_principles.held: However, this power is to be exercised sparingly and with caution.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh vrs. State of Punjab and another, (2014) 6 SCC 466

legal_principles.principle: Guiding factor in quashing criminal proceedings is to secure the ends of justice or prevent abuse of process.
legal_principles.held: When the parties have reached the settlement and on that basis petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding factor in such cases would be to secure: (i) ends of justice, or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any court.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh vrs. State of Punjab and another, (2014) 6 SCC 466

legal_principles.principle: Criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character should be quashed when parties have resolved their disputes.
legal_principles.held: Those criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh vrs. State of Punjab and another, (2014) 6 SCC 466

legal_principles.principle: Offences under Section 307 IPC are generally treated as crimes against society, not individual.
legal_principles.held: Offences under Section 307 IPC would fall in the category of heinous and serious offences and therefore are to be generally treated as crime against the society and not against the individual alone.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh vrs. State of Punjab and another, (2014) 6 SCC 466

outcome.final_order: Criminal proceeding quashed as no useful purpose is going to be served to continue with the same
